items.text: Table IV gives the net increase of the electrolytes in the urine of 0-12 hr after the dose over the 12-0 hr before the dose (results). The pre-dose amounts are not reported, so the totals cannot be recovered; the earlier curation added baselines of Williams1982 (about 7 mmol/hr sodium, 20 mmol/hr chloride, 3.5 mmol/hr potassium). Is 'cumulative amount (change)' the right measurement for a change relative to a pre-dose collection?
items.author: mkoenig

items.text: Added the terminal half-life t1/2beta of Table III (mean ± SD, n = 12) for the 25, 50 and 100 mg tablet and suspension doses; Table III has no 200 mg dose. The paper calculates it as ln 2/beta of the slowest rate constant of a triexponential fit (Eq. 1) to each individual plasma profile and calls it the terminal elimination half-life. The SD is large (up to 8.4 h at a mean of 8.2 h). Values checked twice against the image.
items.author: mkoenig

items.text: Mapped the rate constant beta of Table III to kel in 1/hr. Beta is the slowest exponent of the triexponential fit (Eq. 1) and the paper treats it as the terminal elimination rate (t1/2beta = ln 2/beta). The vocabulary has no separate term for a terminal or lambda_z rate constant. Is kel the right term for beta?
items.author: mkoenig

items.text: The rate constants alpha and gamma and r2 of Table III are only in the raw table. The paper does not say which exponent of Eq. 1 is absorption (gamma, about 0.9-1.3 1/hr, is the fastest), and it says the alpha phase is probably too long for tissue uptake or redistribution, so kabs and kdist would be assumptions; the vocabulary has no term for a coefficient of determination. Should gamma be mapped to kabs or alpha to kdist?
items.author: mkoenig

thread.author: mkoenig
thread.text: Curator decision (mkoenig): alpha, gamma and r2 are not mapped; they stay in the raw table Patel1984_Tab3.tsv.

items.text: The text layer of the PDF reads 0.99 ± 0.31 for gamma of the 50 mg tablet; the image of Table III shows 0.99 ± 0.34 at high zoom, which the raw table keeps.
